title: Claims Manager dashboard
walkthroughSteps: Switch the persona to Tobias Grau (Manager). The dashboard opens on his own claims and his team's, no extra navigation.
The five numbers at the top are filters: click one to jump to the team list filtered to it.
Team workload: one row per direct team member plus the team queue, each with View claims (drill-down).
Every flagged claim shows why: Overdue (task past due), High value (250,000 or more), For review (a handler marked it).
Open a claim and press Back: you return to the same filtered view (filters live in the address).
Decisions on the open questions are in AC notes. Thresholds are placeholders until the business confirms them.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC1 · Own cases, team workload and drill-down into a member
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement:
**Opens:** Dashboard as Tobias Grau (Claims Manager).

**You see:** Role badge Claims Manager, five summary numbers, **My claims** (CLM-2024-021, CLM-2024-102), and **Team workload** for the Property claims team: one row per member (Mara, Lena, Nina, Elke, Dirk, Sabine) plus the team queue. Sabine shows "(Out of office until 28-11-2026)" after her name, from the same user directory as the reassign dialog.

**Try:** Press **View claims** on Lena Zorn: the list below shows only Lena's claims with a **View whole team** link to go back.

Decision (open question 3): a team is the manager's direct reports only, one manager per handler (DESIGN DECISION CM-TEAM-1). Claims with no handler in the team's group show as the **Team queue** row. Team size in the mock: 6 people; the member table has no paging, rows stay one line each so 20 to 30 people stay scannable.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC2 · Flagged claims are highlighted, say why, and can be filtered
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement:
**Opens:** Dashboard as Tobias Grau.

**You see:** Each flag is a badge in the **Needs attention** column (same badge + tooltip as "Review needed" on Sections). Hover a badge for the reason, e.g. on CLM-2024-016 **Overdue** "2 tasks late, oldest due 11-06-2026", **High value** "CHF 250,000 or more", **For review** "Lena Zorn: Coverage question...".

**Try:** Click the **Need attention** number (the list comes into view, headed "Open team claims: Needs attention" with "Showing 8 of 10 claims"), or set **Show** to Overdue / High value / For review: only those claims remain.

**NOTE [accepted-deviation]:** thresholds were open (open question 1). Implemented: Overdue = an open task past its due date; High value = loss amount 250,000 or more in the claim currency (no FX); For review = a handler marked the claim (review-flags.json). See DESIGN DECISION CM-FLAG-1. Treated as `done` pending product sign-off.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC3 · Prioritisation fields, sort and filter by member, status and flag
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement:
**Opens:** Dashboard as Tobias Grau, Team workload.

**You see:** Columns: Claim (with a Closed chip if closed), Client, Handler, Needs attention, Last updated, Loss amount. Filters: Team member, Status, Show (flag). Each list shows its top 8 rows with the count above it ("Showing 8 of 18 claims"), and the heading says which claims they are (e.g. "Open team claims: Overdue", "Lena Zorn's open claims"). **View all claims** in the card header opens the claims list with the same handler and status; the claims list has no team or flag filter, so those are not carried.

**Try:** Click the **Loss amount** header to sort, again to reverse. Amounts are not converted (no exchange rates in the prototype), so claims are grouped by currency and sorted within it; the header tooltip says so. Set Status to All statuses: closed claims show with a Closed chip.

Decision (open question 2): the fields above (DESIGN DECISION CM-FIELDS-1). Default sort: most flags first, so what needs the manager is on top. The Handler column hides once you drill into one person.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC4 · Stale data with last updated and refresh
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement:
**Opens:** Dashboard as Tobias Grau, data two hours old.

**You see:** Warning: "This data is from <time> and may be out of date." with **Refresh now**; the Team workload header shows the same time next to **Refresh**.

**Try:** Press **Refresh now**: the button shows a small spinner for a moment while the page stays where it is, then the warning goes away and the time is now. **Refresh** in the Team workload header works the same way.

Decision (open question 6): data loads when the page opens and on Refresh, no live polling, so rows don't jump while the manager reads. Older than 15 minutes = marked out of date (DESIGN DECISION CM-REFRESH-1).
